g.text: Embedding-based NLP services—including semantic search, text classification,
and language model inference—require transmitting dense vector
representations of user text to remote servers.
g.title: N1 [Context] (cites=0) Embedding-based NLP services—including semantic search, text classification, and language model inference—require transmitting dense vector representations of user text to remote servers.

g.text: Embeddings can be inverted to text
These embeddings, while enabling powerful downstream applications, pose

can be inverted to recover the original text with high fidelity (Morris et
g.title: N2 [Context] (cites=2) These embeddings, while enabling powerful downstream applications, pose significant privacy risks: recent work has demonstrated that text embeddings can be inverted to recover the original text with high fidelity (Morris et al., 2023; Kale et al., 2025).

g.text: This vulnerability is particularly concerning in split inference
architectures, where clients compute embeddings locally before sending them
g.title: N3 [Context] (cites=0) This vulnerability is particularly concerning in split inference architectures, where clients compute embeddings locally before sending them to untrusted servers.

g.text: To mitigate embedding leakage, researchers have proposed perturbation-based
defenses that add calibrated noise to embeddings before transmission.
g.title: N4 [Context] (cites=0) To mitigate embedding leakage, researchers have proposed perturbation-based defenses that add calibrated noise to embeddings before transmission.

g.text: A prominent approach combines L2-Laplacian noise with norm clipping (Mai et
al., 2023), providing dχ-privacy guarantees (Chatzikokolakis et al., 2013)
g.title: N5 [Prior_Work] (cites=2) A prominent approach combines L2-Laplacian noise with norm clipping (Mai et al., 2023), providing dχ-privacy guarantees (Chatzikokolakis et al., 2013) while bounding the output space.

g.title: N6 [Limitation] (cites=0) However, the effectiveness of this defense has been evaluated primarily using simple per-token nearest-neighbor (NN) attacks, which ignore sequence-level constraints.

baselines under input-independent noise—but BeamClean's evaluation did not
g.title: N7 [Limitation] (cites=1) Recent work on BeamClean (Kale et al., 2025) has shown that sequence-aware attacks leveraging language model priors can dramatically outperform NN baselines under input-independent noise—but BeamClean's evaluation did not include norm-clipped mechanisms.

g.title: N8 [Method] (cites=0) This gap raises a critical question: Does the sequence-aware BeamClean attacker pose a greater threat than simple NN decoding under norm-clipped L2-Laplacian perturbation?

g.title: N9 [Method] (cites=0) If BeamClean significantly outperforms NN, then privacy evaluations relying solely on NN attacks may substantially underestimate leakage.

Conversely, if norm clipping closes the gap, it could serve as an effective
g.title: N10 [Method] (cites=0) Conversely, if norm clipping closes the gap, it could serve as an effective practical mitigation.

g.text: We conduct a systematic privacy audit to answer this question, and our
g.title: N11 [Method] (cites=0) We conduct a systematic privacy audit to answer this question, and our findings are surprising.

g.text: At the operating point proposed in prior work (η = 142, producing 30–50%
clip rate), both NN and BeamClean achieve near-perfect reconstruction
g.title: N12 [Result] (cites=0) At the operating point proposed in prior work (η = 142, producing 30–50% clip rate), both NN and BeamClean achieve near-perfect reconstruction (>99.98% Token-ASR, 100% Canary-EM).

g.text: The comparison between attackers becomes moot: the defense provides no
g.title: N13 [Result] (cites=0) The comparison between attackers becomes moot: the defense provides no meaningful privacy protection.

g.text: We demonstrate a ceiling effect: at the proposed operating point,
both simple and sophisticated attackers achieve near-perfect
g.title: C1 [Contribution] (cites=0) We demonstrate a ceiling effect: at the proposed operating point, both simple and sophisticated attackers achieve near-perfect reconstruction, rendering the defense ineffective.

g.text: C2: BeamClean does not beat NN here
We show that BeamClean does not outperform NN under norm-clipped
perturbation; in fact, NN achieves marginally higher accuracy due
g.title: C2 [Contribution] (cites=0) We show that BeamClean does not outperform NN under norm-clipped perturbation; in fact, NN achieves marginally higher accuracy due to the ceiling effect.

g.text: We explain this finding through directional preservation analysis:
norm clipping preserves directional information exactly, making
simple NN attacks sufficient when noise is mild.
g.title: C3 [Contribution] (cites=0) We explain this finding through directional preservation analysis: norm clipping preserves directional information exactly, making simple NN attacks sufficient when noise is mild.
